title: Split-Zero cohomology: geometric weight control, positive quotients and original-character lifts

project.name: Split-Zero cohomology and the zeta-function research programme

scope: A result graph for the latest accepted calculations, with a full source-heading index for their cumulative context. Stated internal proof results and reconstructed classical theorems retain their original domains and review limits. This catalogue is not independent certification of every historical proof in the readers.
human_contribution: The human investigator supplied the originating support construction, mathematical agenda and corrections. Collaborating AI tasks developed the programme calculations; the classical mathematics is attributed to its human sources below and at point of use.

definition_preservation.tau_addition: Retracted; not a premise. No primitive addition, parity or numerical weight is assigned to τ.
definition_preservation.arithmetic_operations: Used only on the separately constructed coefficient and arithmetic objects, with their comparison maps retained.

results.result: Reconstructs determinant and tensor/exterior-power purity, monodromy weights, the strict boundary estimate, and the local invariant-cycle lifting argument in Deligne's stated arithmetic setting, then writes the original-zeta receiving maps.
results.programme_use: Provides the full weight-control mechanism to compare with the programme's actual coefficient geometry, including every degree and Tate factor.
results.scope_limit: The finite-field weight theorem is not thereby transferred to the original-zeta coefficient object.

results.result: Calculates the local nearby-cycle, specialization, dual and signed residue/Gysin maps, with ramification degrees retained. The global shifted-source lift is compatible with a surviving local quotient; the total residue/Gysin class need not vanish on the critical line.
results.programme_use: Separates the calculated topological residue receiver from the receiver of the transfer-adjoint defect, preventing a nonzero geometric class from being treated as an RH violation.
results.scope_limit: No numerical arithmetic weight separation or vanishing of the original adjoint defect is established.

results.result: Constructs the actual invariant-cycle crosses, geometric cover actions with cut corrections and composition homotopies, and the continuous-dual fine resolution with its signs. It retains the original Q boundary map and the complete two-pole global map. The primal obstruction is beta_r(Q), with source Q/Z_r; vanishing of the current-side quotient is independent of that defect.
results.programme_use: Places the measured arithmetic defect in a specific geometric cross and tracks it through the full source, covers and dual, rather than inferring weight vanishing from an auxiliary quotient.
results.scope_limit: The calculations do not establish beta_r(Q)=0, arithmetic purity, or RH.

results.result: For the specified multiplicity-weighted zero-value Hilbert space and original transfer operators, determines the closure of the measured adjoint-defect range as the off-line value sector, constructs the universal positive receiver, and classifies bounded positive forms satisfying the transfer-adjoint relation. The multiplicity trace is distinguished from the ordinary Hilbert operator trace.
results.programme_use: Calculates exactly what positive compression removes, and what any bounded positive receiving intertwiner must kill.
results.scope_limit: The theorem concerns the stated value Hilbert category, not every full-jet form or algebraic receiver. The off-line sector has not been proved empty.

results.result: Retains the higher jets, reconstructs the original source by an explicit fibre product, states the exact closedness criterion for its topological comparison, and computes the arithmetic contribution discarded by the positive quotient. The full identity is W_L(F,G)=A(0)+A(1)+A_infinity(v)-P_hist(v)-W_O(F,G).
results.programme_use: Makes source recovery and the original Weil contribution visible after compression, so positivity of the quotient cannot silently substitute for positivity of the original form.
results.scope_limit: The complementary original term W_O is retained, not proved zero. The topological fibre-product statement retains its exact ideal-sum closedness criterion.

results.result: Computes the complete strong-dual closure of the original Gysin defect image, retains the raw and separated costalk quotients, and identifies the conjugate positive receiver as a literal degree-zero summand. Constructs the restricted original Fréchet source row and its strict strong-dual transpose, proves bounded inverse scale comparisons for r,t>1 and their cocycle law, and retains both labelled endpoint lines and the full coefficient kernel in the receiving triangle.
results.programme_use: Connects the actual geometric Gysin receiver to PTQ's positive receiver through explicit source and quotient maps, including the defect subspace lost in the quotient and every higher-jet contribution.
results.scope_limit: The receiving quotient kills the calculated closed defect image; its existence does not make the original defect vanish. The raw quotient is not replaced by its separated quotient, and the positive image is not asserted to be the entire source dual. Coefficient parameters r>1 are not all geometric cover degrees; that interpretation is reserved for recovered positive integers.

results.result: Constructs triangular lifts of the original Mellin jets through the original summation transpose. For zero order m and jet order j, computes the least generalized-character order m+j+1 in the full dual, with the Fourier-return and reflected block retained.
results.programme_use: Replaces an unspecified lifting interface with the actual coefficients and least required character enlargement.
results.scope_limit: The lifting theorem alone supplies no arithmetic purity estimate or RH conclusion.

results.result: Calculates the original restriction extension, its cyclic resolution, connecting class and full supported-cone comparison, retaining the full Gamma germ and the original dual/twist conventions. The independent sign check records the inverse order in the reflected differential and q(X) to q(1-X).
results.programme_use: Identifies the actual source class to which Deligne's cross is being compared, before any quotient or finite truncation.
results.scope_limit: The geometric weight inequalities are not assumed for this arithmetic receiver.

results.result: Calculates the actual residue image and pushout of the original restriction extension, with coherent sections on the complete locally finite character domain, all real actions, and the supported contribution at the original -1/2 germ.
results.programme_use: Tracks a specified extension class through the complete residue map and quotient; it distinguishes a lift into that quotient from a lift into the original full target.
results.scope_limit: Neither perfectness of an unproved full pairing nor vanishing of the original character defect is inferred from a quotient lift.

results.result: Constructs the degreewise exact quotient of the complete supported comparison, its exact triangle and explicit continuous cone contraction, then calculates the connecting sequence after the cyclic resolution. The graded section is not silently treated as a cochain section.
results.programme_use: Supplies the maps, homotopy and signs needed to compare the original and supported targets without deleting an extension class by notation.
results.scope_limit: Exactness and contraction at this quotient do not establish the missing arithmetic weight separation.

results.result: Identifies the actual specialization obstruction with R=Q/N_O, retaining its Fréchet quotient topology, the strict strong-dual row, both poles and endpoint lines. Calculates the source subcomplex whose transpose produces the separated current receiver and the dense original pairing into its dual.
results.programme_use: Connects ACD's original specialization map to GDC's exact annihilator and strong closure, so the obstruction source has a specified topology before any positive completion.
results.scope_limit: The dense injective Hilbert comparison is not automatically positive-transfer-adjoint, and the source quotient R is not proved zero.

results.result: On the actual Fréchet full-jet quotient Q, every jointly continuous positive semidefinite Hermitian form satisfying B(T_nF,G)=B(F,nT_(1/n)G) for every recovered positive integer n has the unique form sum over Re(rho)=1/2 of m_rho c_rho F(rho) conjugate(G(rho)), with nonnegative polynomially bounded coefficients c_rho. Conversely every such coefficient family gives a continuous compatible form. The proof supplies the unitary spectral decomposition through a positive Fourier-measure argument and retains the complete original-zeta multiplier.
results.programme_use: Closes the earlier PTQ restriction to forms bounded in a preselected value Hilbert norm; the classification now applies to all jointly continuous compatible forms on the original Fréchet source without assuming density of finite primal jets.
results.scope_limit: Every compatible positive receiver kills the calculated higher-jet and off-line-value kernel; the classification does not prove that kernel absent in the original source. The multiplier's endpoint, Gamma, rational and trivial-zero data are retained, not discarded.

results.result: The common radical of all classified forms is N_L. Their countable weighted square-sum seminorms complete Q/N_L to the rapid weighted sequence space S_L, with an explicit dense map and universal continuous Hilbert receiving property. The same completion is obtained from N_O/N_0 using the inherited seminorms. For the actual specialization quotient R=Q/N_O, every continuous compatible positive form is zero: P(R)={0}.
results.programme_use: Calculates what the entire positive receiving category sees of the original source and of its actual specialization obstruction, with the full strict source/dual row retained.
results.scope_limit: P(R)={0} does not imply R=0. The generated positive-seminorm topology is not identified with the original Fréchet topology. No extension theorem for every form intrinsic to N_O is claimed. The original Weil complement W_O remains explicit.

connections.meaning: The source theorem supplies the pattern of the invariant-cycle cross; the programme constructs its actual source maps without importing the numerical weight inequalities.
Local boundary and signed residue calculations are retained in the later defect cross and full cover action.
PSC calculates the full-jet source and the original arithmetic term omitted by the PTQ value compression.
GDC applies to the retained RGR current receiver and computes its exact image closure, source annihilator and raw/separated costalks.
The Gysin costalk's degree-zero summand is the conjugate PTQ receiver; the degree-one raw quotient, endpoint lines and full coefficient kernel are kept.
AST identifies the original-source obstruction quotient and its topology using the retained ADC/ACD maps, not a new positive quotient chosen in advance.
The GDC annihilator and strong closure are the transpose data of AST's actual strict source row.
CFP removes the earlier assumption of boundedness for the value Hilbert norm and classifies all jointly continuous positive transfer forms on the actual source.
The full coefficient classification determines the common radical and rapid weighted sequence completion.
The classification is pulled back along the actual quotient Q to R=Q/N_O; the original isolators force every compatible positive form on R to vanish, without proving R=0.
Actual lifted jets and their least generalized order supply the original extension calculation, retaining zero multiplicity.
RPC sends the original connecting class through the specified residue image; quotient and full-target lifts remain distinct.
The same class is followed through the full supported complex and its exact quotient triangle, with signs and contraction explicit.

human_sources.title: 245B, Notes 5: Hilbert spaces
human_sources.use: The inspected exposition proves the complex Hilbert-space Riesz representation theorem and identifies the continuous linear dual with the conjugate Hilbert space. ADC8 and ACD1 retain this conjugate-space convention in their explicit source and continuous-dual formulas. The programme-specific maps are not attributed to this classical source.

human_sources.title: 245C, Notes 2: The Fourier transform
human_sources.use: The positive-definite Fourier-measure representation used and reproved in CFPA is classical Bochner theory, not a new theorem of the programme. The Gaussian argument also uses Fourier inversion with its displayed source conventions retained. CFP applies that mechanism to its retained original-zeta source multiplier; CPS uses the resulting source classification.
human_sources.reading_scope: The publication pass verified Theorem 57 and displayed equation (11), not the complete Fourier-transform lecture or Bochner's original paper.

human_sources.title: 245B, Notes 12: Continuous functions on locally compact Hausdorff spaces
human_sources.use: The measure representation of a positive functional on C_c as a Radon measure is used inside the CFPA positive Fourier-measure proof. This classical measure representation is distinct from the Hilbert-space conjugate-dual Riesz theorem used in ADC/ACD.
human_sources.reading_scope: The publication coordinator verified Theorem 24, not the entire lecture or the original historical sources.
